title: Fix Release workflow (release-plz): PR creation blocked, orphan branches spam

comments.author: example-user
comments.text: Diagnosis (attempt B): the Release workflow (release.yml) has failed on all 47 runs. Failure: release-plz pushes a `chore: release vX.Y.Z` branch, then fails to open the release PR with HTTP 403 from `POST /repos/example-org/example-repo/pulls`: "GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests." Repo Actions setting `can_approve_pull_request_reviews=false` (Settings -> Actions -> General -> Workflow permissions) blocks GITHUB_TOKEN from creating PRs. Side effect: 46 orphaned `release-plz-<timestamp>` branches, one per failed run. Publishing config is fine: release-plz.toml publish=false, so no CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN needed. Trigger (push to main only) is correct for GitFlow. Fix: pre-flight permission check that skips release-plz with an explicit warning when PR creation is blocked; release-plz.toml semver_check=false (crate never published to crates.io, registry semver baseline unavailable).

comments.author: example-user
comments.text: Superseded — BotSpy releases directly with no release PR (the maintainer's decision); the direct-release rework is being done by attempt A. Note: the reconciled fix (PR #3, combining this task's pre-flight skip with attempt A's RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN override) was merged to develop (8a74af6) just before the stop instruction arrived; it is inert on develop since Release only triggers on main. Root cause stays valid for the direct-release rework: repo setting 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests' is disabled (can_approve_pull_request_reviews=false) and no RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN secret exists — one of those must be unlocked for any GITHUB_TOKEN/PAT-based release flow.

comments.author: example-user
comments.text: Closed as superseded — direct-release rework owned by attempt A per the maintainer's decision
